- Our business is dependent and will continue to depend on our manufacturing facility, and we are subject to certain risks in our manufacturing process.
- Any slowdown or shutdown in our manufacturing operations or strikes, work stoppages or increased wage demands by our employees that could interfere with our operations could have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.
- We operate from our manufacturing facility situated at Khatwad Tal, Dindori Dist, Nashik, Maharashtra which is spread across approximately 5100 sq. mts.
- The core of our business relies on efficient management of the manufacturing facility, however our operations face several operational risks, some of which are beyond our control, such as the breakdown, failure of equipment or industrial accidents, severe weather conditions and natural disasters.
- Further, we may be subject to manufacturing disruptions due to contraventions by us of any of the conditions of our regulatory approvals, which may require our manufacturing facilities to cease, or limit, production until the disputes concerning such approvals are resolved.
- While we have not encountered significant disruptions at our manufacturing facilities in recent years, we did experience a decline in production during 2020 due to the challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic.
- While we have since recovered, we cannot guarantee that future disruptions will not occur.
- Our inability to effectively respond to such events and rectify any disruption, in a timely manner and at an acceptable cost, could lead to the slowdown or shutdown of our operations or the under-utilization of our manufacturing facilities, which in turn may have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations. 2.

orders_not_placed.note: Affirmative disclosure, verbatim: 'We have considered the above quotations for the budgetary estimate purpose and have not placed orders for them. The actual cost of procurement and actual supplier/dealer may vary.' The statement covers the whole quotation table, so all 12 line items aggregating the printed total of Rs 515.91 lakhs (Rs 514.91 lakhs IPO-funded) are unordered - 100% of the capital expenditure. The Company adds that it has 'not entered into any definitive agreements with any of the vendor and there can be no assurance that the same vendor would be engaged to eventually supply the machineries or at the same costs', that management retains flexibility to change vendor or add/modify/delete machineries at the time of actual placement of order, that no second-hand machinery is being acquired, and that the Promoters, Directors and KMP have no interest in the quoting entities. QUOTATION VALIDITY vs DEPLOYMENT: the RHP states 'Quotation received from the vendor mentioned above is valid as on the date of this Red Herring Prospectus' (cover-dated August 24, 2026), but every quotation validity date falls between September 30, 2026 and October 15, 2026 - i.e. all 12 quotations, and therefore 100% of the Rs 515.91 lakhs capex, expire within about seven weeks of the RHP date while the entire deployment is scheduled across Fiscal 2027 (ending March 31, 2027). The RHP acknowledges the consequence: quotations 'are valid for a specific period of time and may lapse after the expiry of the said period. Consequent upon which, there could be a possible escalation in the cost'. TENSION TO NOTE: an 'Advance already paid - Internal Accruals' of Rs 1.00 lakh is deducted from the Rs 515.91 lakhs total, i.e. an advance has been paid against machinery for which the notes state no orders have been placed; the RHP does not identify which line item the advance relates to. Risk Factor 26 describes the same capital expenditure as 'We have estimated the total cost towards these capital expenditures for Rs 514.91 lakhs', whereas the Objects table prints Rs 515.91 lakhs as the total cost and Rs 514.91 lakhs as the IPO-funded balance.

concerns_observed: Supplier concentration is severe and structural: the single largest supplier was 62.60% of total purchases in FY26 (2,919.30 of 4,663.53 lakhs), 64.57% in FY25 and 61.30% in FY24, with top-5 at 80.48%; the RHP states there are no long-term supply contracts or fixed-price agreements with any raw-material supplier, and one material creditor of 200.38 lakhs is about 55% of the 364.37 lakhs of trade payables owed to 38 creditors.

Growth mix deteriorated in FY26: of the 616.21 lakh increase in revenue from operations (derived, 5,030.32 to 5,646.53), 252.21 lakhs (41%, derived) came from the unspecified 'Other Trading' line rising 40.28 to 292.49 lakhs, described only as polymer products, custom moulded tanks, moulds, mechanical and industrial spares and consumables; manufactured revenue grew 7.2% (4,878.30 to 5,229.31 lakhs).

Lender concentration bears on the Issue itself: Kotak Mahindra Bank holds 490.35 of the 590.62 lakhs outstanding (83%), its cash-credit sanction requires the entire banking, foreign-exchange and bill business to be routed through KMBL under sole banking, and both KMBL and SIDBI require prior permission for any change in shareholding, directorship or ownership.

Export revenue declined in absolute terms for three consecutive years, 1,456.91 to 1,418.82 to 1,316.78 lakhs (31.02% to 28.21% to 23.32% of revenue from operations) while total revenue rose; the Company states it undertakes no foreign-currency hedging, and unrealised FX swung from an 11.71 lakh gain in FY24 to a 9.21 lakh loss in FY26.

The sole manufacturing site (about 5,100 sq. mts. at Gat No. 172, Khatwad, Dindori, Nashik) is leased from promoter Ulka Umakant Savadekar under a lease deed dated November 06, 2015; Annexure-AJ(xii) records the office and factory building as constructed over leasehold land and the Company owns no immovable property, with 61 related-party rows disclosed in Annexure-AD.

Promoter group includes one body corporate, Heera Roto Compounds Private Limited, and one partnership firm, M/s Alkemy India (Umakant and Ulka Savadekar as partners); the RHP affirmatively states there are no Group Companies under its September 20, 2025 materiality policy, so neither appears in Annexure-AD and no revenue, PAT or health data is given for either.
Domestic sales are concentrated in the home state: Maharashtra was 3,083.06 lakhs of FY26 revenue from operations, about 55% of the total (derived), against Karnataka 246.16 and Gujarat 164.78 lakhs.

Statutory-dues delays are quantified inside the restated accounts: interest on income tax of 10.78 / 4.30 / 2.77 lakhs, interest on TDS of 0.30 / nil / 0.02, interest on MSME dues of 2.91 / 2.19 / nil, and a section 36(1)(va) disallowance of 0.40 / 0.04 / 1.54 lakhs for FY26 / FY25 / FY24 (Annexure-AI), alongside 18 / 16 / 23 instances of delayed EPF, ESI, professional tax and labour welfare fund payments in Risk Factor 20.

Filing quality shows text carried over from unrelated documents: external Risk Factor 7 warns about regulations affecting 'the ceramic tableware industry or the HORECA sector that we primarily serve', and external Risk Factor 1 refers to 'the date of this Draft Red Herring Prospectus' inside a Red Herring Prospectus dated August 24, 2026.
data_gaps: No price band, issue price, general-corporate-purpose amount or aggregate issue size is filled in this RHP: every such field prints '[bullet]', the Objects table 'Total' row is a placeholder and the schedule-of-implementation total row is blank. The three quantified objects are 250.00 (debt repayment) plus 514.91 (machinery) plus 300.00 (working capital) = 1,064.91 lakhs, a derived sum the RHP itself does not print. The cap the RHP states on general corporate purposes is a regulatory ceiling expressed as a percentage-or-absolute limit, not an allocation, and no general-corporate-purpose amount is disclosed.

No listed-peer comparison exists because the issuer affirmatively states, twice under 'Basis for Offer Price', that no listed Indian company is engaged in a similar business; consequently no peer accounting-ratio table, no peer RoNW, EPS or NAV, and the industry price-multiple block that would normally accompany a peer set is absent rather than blank. This is an issuer disclosure, not a missing table.

No market size, market share or addressable-market figure for rotational-moulding compounds appears in this record: market_position.share_pct is null and the positioning is stated only qualitatively as niche.

No order book, orders-in-hand, unexecuted-order value or letter of intent is disclosed anywhere in the 328-page document, verified by an exhaustive sweep of the staged full text across all 26 sections. This is an absence of disclosure, not an issuer statement that no forward book exists; the Company does state it typically does not enter long-term customer agreements.

No top-5 customer concentration figure is disclosed anywhere (a top-5 tier is given for suppliers only), so the tier between the 15.73% top-1 and the 52.99% top-10 cannot be sized. Absence of disclosure, not a nil.

No stub or interim period is presented: the restated financials cover only FY2024, FY2025 and FY2026 (approved by the Board on July 16, 2026), so nothing after March 31, 2026 is audited even though the RHP is dated August 24, 2026. This is the document's own presentation, not an extraction gap.

Seasonality is effectively undisclosed: the statutory item cross-references the Industry Overview and Our Business chapters, neither of which discusses seasonality, and no quarterly, half-yearly or monthly revenue or production split appears anywhere.

The Advance Authorisation licence carries no licence number, issue date, export-obligation quantum or expiry anywhere in the document and is not itemised in the Government and Other Approvals chapter, so the outstanding export obligation cannot be sized.

The names and amounts of material creditors are stated to be available on the Company's website and expressly do not form part of the RHP, so the 200.38 lakh single material creditor cannot be identified from the document.
Cash and bank balances of 69.18 lakhs include deposits pledged as margin money against loans, bank guarantees and letters of credit; the RHP does not split free from encumbered cash.

GST dues delays are asserted in the Risk Factor 20 narrative ('minor delays in payment of GST, ESIC, PF, IT and other statutory dues in the past') but the quantified table covers only EPF, ESI, professional tax and labour welfare fund; the GST delays are not quantified anywhere.

No revenue, PAT or financial-health information is given for promoter-group entities Heera Roto Compounds Private Limited or M/s Alkemy India, neither of which is disclosed as a Group Company or appears in Annexure-AD.

The Company's own Annexure-AD outstanding-balances table prints 'Against Reimbursement of Expenses - Mrs. Ulka Umakant Savadekar 0.07' with no indication of which of the three year-end columns it belongs to; the defect is identical in both printed copies of the annexure.

verdict.our_read: Single-plant Nashik maker of rotational-moulding polymer compounds (FY26 revenue 5,646.53 lakhs, PAT 408.90 lakhs, EBITDA margin 10.78%, 33 employees) whose thesis rides on converting profit into cash: FY26 operating cash flow was 19% of PAT on a 332.90 lakh inventory build.

parameter_scores.basis: FY26 CFO of 78.00 lakhs is 19% of PAT of 408.90 lakhs; cumulative three-year CFO of 597.22 against PAT of 862.46 is 69% (derived from the printed cash-flow series). Working capital absorbed 505.53 in FY26 on a 332.90 inventory build and 137.41 receivables build; inventory days went 35 to 45 to 62 and printed inventory turnover fell 11.10 to 9.44 to 7.18. The working-capital gap widened 603.58 to 771.00 to 1,248.19 lakhs.

Quarterly stock statements to Kotak Mahindra Bank disagree with the books in all twelve quarters of FY24 to FY26 (Annexure-F(c)), largest disclosed differences 92.29, 83.19, 81.01 and 77.51 lakhs. Annexure-AJ(xiii) states no charge filings are pending while Risk Factor 12 admits Form CHG-1 was never filed (section 77). Sixteen RoC forms filed late, including eight MSME half-yearly returns up to four years late. Restatement (Annexure-V) cut audited PAT by 50.41 lakhs in FY25 and 2.85 lakhs in FY24, covering gratuity moved from cash to AS-15 actuarial basis, subsidy recognised on receipt, and insurance/AMC on cash basis.

Largest supplier 62.60% / 64.57% / 61.30% of total purchases and top-5 80.48% / 80.27% / 77.32%, with no long-term or fixed-price supply contracts; the RHP's own Risk Factor 3 heading concedes the single largest supplier exceeded 50% in each of the last three fiscals. On the demand side the concentration is milder (top-1 15.73%, top-10 52.99%) but the Company states it typically does not enter long-term customer agreements, and no order book is disclosed anywhere in the document.

The RHP states twice, under 'Basis for Offer Price', that no listed Indian company is engaged in a similar business, so no peer-comparison table and no peer accounting ratios are printed (affirmative issuer disclosure, no_peer_flag set). No market size, market share or addressable-market figure for rotational-moulding compounds appears in the record: market_position.share_pct is null and positioning is stated only qualitatively as niche, with competition described as 'various large and small manufactures' in organised and unorganised structures.

100% of the 515.91 lakh machinery capex is un-ordered ('We have considered the above quotations for the budgetary estimate purpose and have not placed orders for them'), all 12 quotations lapse between September 30 and October 15, 2026 against deployment across Fiscal 2027, and a 1.00 lakh advance has been paid against machinery for which no orders exist. No object has been appraised and no monitoring agency is appointed. Both of those are LAWFUL here and affirmatively stated, not omissions: appraisal is not mandatory, and Regulation 262(1) does not require a monitoring agency for an issue up to 5,000 lakhs, stated consistently in three places, with the Audit Committee monitoring under Regulation 32 instead. The score reflects execution readiness, not pricing, on a document that sets no price.

parameter_scores.basis: Text from unrelated filings survives (ceramic tableware/HORECA in external RF 7; 'Draft Red Herring Prospectus' in external RF 1). Recorded self-contradictions include: the 1%-or-more table printing a total of 75,39,922 shares against line items summing to 73,13,154; Regulation 238(b) lock-in tranches out by one share (44,49,153 vs 44,49,154); RF 51 assigning 64.05% to Promoters plus Promoter Group where note 16 assigns it to Promoters alone (72.56% for the combined group); one woman director versus three in the same chapter; Trading revenue printed as both 405.65 and 405.64; and the auditors' report citing CARO qualifications and 'the emphasis of matter above' while Annexure-IV note 14 reports Auditor Qualifications as NIL for all three years and no emphasis-of-matter paragraph appears in the report as extracted.

Single leased plant, 33 permanent employees, 89.78% of FY26 revenue from one product family (roto-moulding compound, of which Color Powders alone is 45.55%), not backward integrated into resin, with no long-term contracts on either side and no disclosed order book. Offsetting: in-house laboratory and QC, customisation across nine compound grades, ISO 9001:2015, One Star Export House, sales into about 21 countries and 24 Indian states, and supplementary tank, jobwork and distribution streams.

Pure fresh issue with no OFS and no pledge is aligned. Against that: a 25:1 bonus of 72,50,000 shares on September 20, 2025 falls inside the 18 months preceding the RHP dated August 24, 2026, which the RHP concedes in 'Basis for Issue Price'; promoters' average cost of acquisition is 0.05, 0.00, 0.38 and 0.38 rupees against 10 face value (the issuer's own Risk Factor 50); 2,26,768 shares moved from the two main promoters at 52 rupees per share on August 01, 2026, three weeks before the RHP; and the sole plant is leased from a promoter.

Printed debt-equity 0.82 / 0.47 / 0.43 and current ratio 1.26 / 1.52 / 1.77; total debt 590.63 lakhs against a derived net worth of 1,378.83 lakhs; DSCR 3.23 in FY26; no continuing default and not a wilful defaulter (Annexure-C notes 1 and 3). Qualifiers: cash of 69.18 lakhs includes deposits pledged as margin money against loans, guarantees and letters of credit; 323.99 lakhs (54.9%) of the book is floating rate; and all facilities carry promoter personal guarantees or co-borrower obligations.

Revenue 4,696.93 to 5,030.32 to 5,646.53 lakhs, EBITDA 275.78 to 436.87 to 608.66 (margin 5.87% to 10.78%), PAT 169.39 to 284.17 to 408.90, PAT margin 3.61% to 7.24%, printed RoCE 23.27% to 32.73%. Margins, RoNW, EPS, NAV and the EBITDA bridge all reproduce from the printed statements. Held below 9 because FY25 PBT includes a 3.50 net exceptional credit (fire loss 77.48 less insurance claim 80.98) and the FY25 audited PAT was restated down by 50.41 lakhs.

red_flags: Cash conversion broke down in the year that carries the growth story: FY26 CFO of 78.00 lakhs against PAT of 408.90 lakhs is 19%, and cumulative three-year CFO of 597.22 against PAT of 862.46 lakhs is 69% (derived from the printed cash-flow statements). The gap is fully explained inside the printed statement by a 332.90 lakh inventory build (days 45 to 62) and a 137.41 lakh receivables build, but the FY24 comparison is stark: CFO was 157% of PAT that year.

Quarterly returns and stock statements submitted to Kotak Mahindra Bank against the working-capital facilities disagree with the books of account in all twelve quarters of FY2024, FY2025 and FY2026 (Annexure-F(c)); the largest disclosed differences are 92.29 lakhs on trade payables (FY26 Q2), 83.19 lakhs on inventory (FY25 Q4), 81.01 lakhs on trade receivables (FY26 Q2) and 77.51 lakhs on inventory (FY26 Q1). The RHP records management's explanations and discloses no lender or regulatory action.

100% of the 515.91 lakh plant-and-machinery capex is un-ordered against quotations that expire before deployment: the RHP states orders have not been placed and no definitive vendor agreements exist, yet all 12 quotations carry validity dates between September 30 and October 15, 2026 (oldest quotation dated January 16, 2026) while the entire deployment is scheduled through Fiscal 2027, and a 1.00 lakh advance has already been paid against machinery for which the same note says no orders exist. The RHP itself concedes the quotations 'may lapse' with 'a possible escalation in the cost'.

The restatement materially reduced previously audited profit: Annexure-V records a net adjustment to PAT of minus 50.41 lakhs for FY2025 (17.7% of the restated FY25 PAT of 284.17, derived) and minus 2.85 lakhs for FY2024, spanning gratuity accounted on a cash basis instead of AS-15 actuarial valuation, subsidy income recognised on receipt rather than accrual, a GST demand adjustment, depreciation rate and capitalisation-date errors, and insurance, subscription and AMC expenses on a cash basis.

Two documented governance contradictions the RHP does not reconcile: Annexure-AJ(xiii) states no registration, modification or satisfaction of charge was pending with the Registrar of Companies, while Risk Factor 12 admits Form CHG-1 was never filed for a vehicle-loan charge and calls it a section 77 non-compliance; and the auditors' examination report at paragraph 7(ii) refers to CARO qualifications and 'the emphasis of matter above' while Annexure-IV note 14 reports Auditor Qualifications as NIL for all three years and no emphasis-of-matter paragraph appears in the report as extracted.

Auditor churn immediately before the listing process: Suyog Kadam & Associates resigned as statutory auditor on July 28, 2025 'due to pre-occupation' and Sanvy & Associates was appointed on August 02, 2025, six days later, to secure a peer-reviewed auditor; separately, the restated financial information was prepared by a third firm, Mansaka Ravi & Associates (FRN 015023C, report dated July 16, 2026), which is not the statutory auditor, the RHP citing the statutory auditor's existing commitments.
strengths_observed: EBITDA margin expanded 5.87% to 8.68% to 10.78% (275.78, 436.87, 608.66 lakhs) as revenue rose 4,696.93 to 5,030.32 to 5,646.53 lakhs, with cost of goods sold falling from 81.47% to 78.13% to 76.70% of revenue from operations.

PAT rose 169.39 to 284.17 to 408.90 lakhs (+141% over two years, derived from the printed series); the RHP's printed RoNW of 24.70% / 29.30% / 29.66% and RoCE of 23.27% / 31.99% / 32.73% both reproduce against the restated statements, RoNW checking against a derived net worth of 1,378.83 lakhs (share capital 754.00 plus reserves 624.83).

Pure fresh issue of up to 27,00,000 shares with no offer-for-sale component, and an affirmative statement that no promoter shares are pledged (Capital Structure notes 14 and 26); printed debt-equity fell 0.82 to 0.47 to 0.43 (Annexure-AH) and printed DSCR rose 1.85 to 2.71 to 3.23, while promoters go 86.99% to 64.05%.

Fifteen arithmetic identity checks on the restated accounts tie: the balance sheet closes at 2,532.08 / 2,074.89 / 1,782.56 lakhs, EPS of 5.42 / 3.77 / 2.25 reproduces PAT on 75,40,000 weighted shares, NAV reproduces net worth on both printed bases (18.29 and 334.46), cash flow A+B+C reconciles to each closing cash balance, and the eleven-facility loan schedule ties to 590.62 against balance-sheet debt of 590.63.

Roto-moulding compound capacity was raised 4,100 to 6,000 MTPA between FY24 and FY25 with production up 3,126 to 3,596 to 3,927 MT and tanks running at 91.45% (1,829 of 2,000); every printed utilisation percentage reconciles to production divided by installed capacity per the Sunil Bhor & Associates chartered-engineer certificate dated July 08, 2026.

Customer base is broad for an SME: largest customer 15.73% of FY26 revenue from operations (14.34% FY25, 13.43% FY24) and top-10 52.99%, across about 24 global and about 265 domestic customers in Fiscal 2026 with repeat orders from about 142 customers over three years.

Contingent liabilities are small and fully disclosed: 2.35 lakhs of TDS-default matters at March 31, 2026 plus a 62.26 lakh capital commitment, together 4.69% of net worth, with nil claims not acknowledged as debt and nil guarantees at all three balance-sheet dates.

Disclosed litigation exposure is minimal: five direct-tax TDS-default matters against the Company aggregating 2.35 lakhs and one direct-tax matter of 5.31 lakhs against promoter-director Nivrutti Sonu Savdekar, both below the Board's July 20, 2026 materiality threshold of 14.37 lakhs. The 164.42 lakh civil matter (Civil M.A. 637 of 2022, Jalgaon) is a compensation claim filed BY director Ulka Umakant Savadekar against the National Highway Authority of India and is not an exposure of the issuer, so it is not aggregated with the two exposures above.

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Our business is dependent and will continue to depend on our manufacturing facility, and we are subject to certain risks in our manufacturing process.
- Any slowdown or shutdown in our manufacturing operations or strikes, work stoppages or increased wage demands by our employees that could interfere with our operations could have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.
- We operate from our manufacturing facility situated at Khatwad Tal, Dindori Dist, Nashik, Maharashtra which is spread across approximately 5100 sq. mts.
- The core of our business relies on efficient management of the manufacturing facility, however our operations face several operational risks, some of which are beyond our control, such as the breakdown, failure of equipment or industrial accidents, severe weather conditions and natural disasters.
- Further, we may be subject to manufacturing disruptions due to contraventions by us of any of the conditions of our regulatory approvals, which may require our manufacturing facilities to cease, or limit, production until the disputes concerning such approvals are resolved.
- While we have not encountered significant disruptions at our manufacturing facilities in recent years, we did experience a decline in production during 2020 due to the challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic.
- While we have since recovered, we cannot guarantee that future disruptions will not occur.
- Our inability to effectively respond to such events and rectify any disruption, in a timely manner and at an acceptable cost, could lead to the slowdown or shutdown of our operations or the under-utilization of our manufacturing facilities, which in turn may have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations. 2.
